summary: Test-only change for TM-09 (session and memory isolation). test/selftest_sessions.py gains route-inventory tests that enumerate every route under /v1/skirnir/sessions from the built API app (17+ method/template pairs): without credentials each answers 401 and no owner-scoped store method is called (health() from the store lifecycle is excluded by signature: only methods whose first parameter is owner count); with a valid client of the same project who does not own the session (store returns NOT_FOUND), no session-scoped route answers 2xx and every owner-scoped store call receives the authenticated caller. test/selftest_memory.py enumerates every route under /v1/skirnir/memory and /v1/skirnir/hindsight: under enforce all answer 401; under observe none answers 2xx and well-formed recall/retain requests reach the identity check and get 401; the memory backend and inference upstream receive no call. Observed behaviour, not a defect: under observe the memory handlers validate the body before checking identity, so a malformed body gets 400 instead of 401; no backend access happens either way. No router code, workflow, configuration or policy change.

findings.evidence: Session/memory isolation was tested for selected routes only; a route added later had no automatic coverage.
findings.resolution: Route-inventory tests with fault-injection evidence; token/grant rotation, the gateway with the gateway enabled and deployment coverage remain, so TM-09 stays open.

tests.command: Fault injection: session GET reads with a fixed owner 'alice' (session_api.py, reverted)
Fault injection: memory.scope_for treats an unauthenticated request as client-a (memory.py, reverted)
tests.evidence: FAIL observe recall 200 != 401 and retain 202 != 401 (plus the existing test_auth_and_client_owned_memory).

limitations: The memory-gateway routes are disabled in the memory harness (404 under observe); under enforce the middleware refuses them; their owner scoping with the gateway enabled is not part of this inventory.
Token and grant rotation and deployment checks are not covered.
